ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.claim: Disbelievers mock the description of Hell because they presume to know everything, but it rests on divine wisdom: truth-seekers benefit and arrogant know-it-alls ruin their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.anchor: Those who have the desire for the truth will benefit from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p46/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p46/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p46/r3.claim: The flames burn criminals' skin from a distance, showing how intense the torment's onset is; 70:16 likewise says it strips the skin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p46/r3.anchor: the skin of the criminals will start to burn even from a distance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r5.claim: The verb lāḥa means to alter or change one's appearance, with poetry describing heat or thirst doing so; al-Akhfash says اللوح is intense thirst.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r5.anchor: لاحه البسر: غير خلقته، قال: تقول ما لاحك يا مسافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses اللوح as severe thirst that changes a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p323/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش: اللوح: شدة العطش، لاحه العطش

FARRA:v3p203/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p203/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p203/r2.claim: The Fire's scorching blackens the skin.
FARRA:v3p203/r2.anchor: وقوله: لواحة للبشر (29) . تسود البشرة بإحراقها.

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r13.claim: ‘Al-bashar’ is the plural of ‘bashara’; Saqar burns the skin until it turns black.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r13.anchor: البشر جمع بشرة، أي تحرق الجلد حتى يسود.

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r1.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r1.claim: Al-Layth says the root means to change something, as thirst changes a person; thus lawwāḥa means “changing.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r1.anchor: قال الليث : لاحه العطش ولوحه إذا غيره ، فاللواحة هي المغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the change as the Fire blackening human skin through burning.

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r3.speaker: الحسن والأصك
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Aṣakk say it appears visibly to people from a distance of five hundred years.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r3.anchor: وهو قول الحسن والأصك : أن معنى اللواحة أنها تلوح للبشر من مسيرة خمسمائة عام

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r4.claim: On this second reading, lawwāḥa derives from lāḥa, “to shine,” as a thing gleams like lightning.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r4.anchor: ولواحة على هذا القول : من لاح الشيء يلوح إذا لمع نحو البرق

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r5.claim: Rāzī compares the Fire’s appearing to those who see it with the statement that Hell is brought into view for all to see.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r5.anchor: وهو كقوله : { وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى } ( النازعات : 36 )

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r6.speaker: القائلون بهذا الوجه
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r6.claim: Proponents of the visible-from-afar reading object that blackening skin conflicts with the next verse’s statement that the Fire neither spares nor leaves anything.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r6.anchor: وطعن القائلون بهذا الوجه في الوجه الأول ، وقالوا : إنه لا يجوز أن يصفها بتسويد البشرة مع قوله إنها : { لا تبقى ولا تذر } ( المدثر : 28 )

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r7.claim: A reading vocalizes lawwāḥa in the accusative as an emphatic specification, heightening terror.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#6/r7.anchor: المسألة الثانية : قرىء : { لواحة } نصبا على الاختصاص للتهويل

STUDYQURAN:74:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r1.speaker: Bg, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r1.claim: The scorching burns the skin until it turns black.
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r1.anchor: Scorching indicates that it burns the skin until it becomes black

STUDYQURAN:74:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r2.speaker: Bg, Q
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r2.claim: Lawwāḥah can also mean something that makes clear: Saqar is made apparent to humanity.
STUDYQURAN:74:29/r2.anchor: which can also indicate something that makes clear, indicating that Saqar is made clear to human beings

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r1.claim: Lawwāḥa means that Saqar changes the skin of its inhabitants.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r1.anchor: وقوله: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] يعني جل ثناؤه مغيرة لبشر أهلها

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī treats lawwāḥa as a description of Saqar and says its nominative is apt despite its indefiniteness because it conveys praise.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r2.anchor: واللواحة من نعت سقر، وبالرد عليها رفعت، وحسن الرفع فيها، وهي نكرة، وسقر معرفة، لما فيها من معنى المدح

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r4.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r4.claim: Abū Razīn says its scorching leaves the skin darker than night.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r4.anchor: عن أبي رزين {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] قال: تلفح الجلد لفحة، فتدعه أشد سوادا من الليل

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says their bodies show upon it.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r5.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] أي: تلوح أجسادهم عليها

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r6.claim: Qatāda says it is scorching heat for the skin.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] أي حراقة للجلد

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it burns a person’s skin.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] يقول: تحرق بشرة الإنسان

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fire changes and burns skin, changing people’s colors; he cites usage for alteration by exposure to the sky.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] قال: تغير البشر، تحرق البشر؛ يقال: قد لاحه استقباله السماء

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains that it burns human skin.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r9.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] يعني بشر الإنسان

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r10.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās calls the skin exposed; al-Ṭabarī suspects this wording is corrupted and should mean changed.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {لواحة للبشر} [المدثر: 29] يقول: معرضة

TAB-FULL:v23p434/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī suspects the transmitted word maʿriḍa is a copying error for mughayyira, meaning changing.
TAB-FULL:v23p434/r11.anchor: وأن يكون موضع معرضة مغيرة، لكن صحف فيه

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r9.claim: Lawwaha derives from changing a person’s complexion to blackness.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r9.anchor: اللواحة من التلويح بمعنى تغيير اللون إلى السواد

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r10.claim: A reported alternative takes the color change to be redness.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r10.anchor: اللواحة من التلويح بمعنى تغيير اللون إلى السواد وقيل إلى الحمرة

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r11.claim: Bashar means the visible outer skin, and بشر is the plural of بشرة.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r11.anchor: والبشر جمع بشرة بمعنى ظاهر الجلد

TABRISI:74:25-31/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:25-31/r10.claim: Another gloss says it scorches skin until it becomes darker than night.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r10.anchor: وقيل: لافحة للجلود حتى تدعها أشد سوادا من الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r1.claim: Al-Layth says thirst, cold, illness, and grief can alter someone; an unattributed line uses the verb of grief changing a person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r1.anchor: قال الليث: (لاحه العطش ولوحه إذا غيره، والتاح إذا عطش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r2.claim: An unattributed line uses laḥa for being changed, saying grief for a dead child, brother, or father had not changed the woman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r2.anchor: ولم يلحها حزن على ابنم ... ولا أخ ولا أب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses lawwāḥa as changing and cites a line about scorching summer winds altering the speaker’s cousin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r4.claim: Al-bashar is the plural of bashara, meaning skin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Fire blackens the skin of whoever is cast into it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني تسود بشرة من يطرح فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r6.speaker: أبو رزين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r6.claim: Abu Razin says its blast sears the skin and leaves it blacker than night.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r7.claim: Muqatil interprets the phrase as burning the skin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r8.claim: He says “burning the skin” conveys the effect rather than a full tafsir: fire pierces and alters the skin until it blackens.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: محرقة للجلد (¬4) -وهو معنى، وليس بتفسير-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r9.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r9.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that it is visible to its inhabitants from five hundred years away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r9.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يلوح لأهلها من مسيرة خمسمائة عام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r10.speaker: الحسن، ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r10.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan also hold that it shines to its inhabitants from five hundred years away.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r11.claim: On this reading lawwāḥa means shining like lightning, and al-bashar means people rather than skins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p433/r11.anchor: ليس المراد بها الجلود، وإنما معناها الناس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r1.claim: Saqar burns the skin until it turns black.

QASHANI:74:29-31/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r1.claim: The fire blackens outward bodies according to their sins and evil dispositions, just as physical fire changes colors and forms.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r1.anchor: مغيرة لظواهر الأجساد إلى لون سواد خطاياهم وهيئات سيئاتهم وذلك من خاصية تلك النار كما تغير النار الجسمانية الألوان والهيئات

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r5.claim: Bashar can mean human beings or the outer surfaces of skin, especially human skin; humans are called bashar for this visible skin.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r5.anchor: derinin bâhusus insan derisinin dış yüzleri mânasına da olur

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r6.claim: Lawwaha is an intensive form of lawh, whose senses include thirst, solar heat, scorching or darkening a face, appearing, flashing, or seeing.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r6.anchor: mübalağa sîgasıdır. “Levh” susamak veya Güneş’in harâreti

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r7.claim: The phrase can picture Saqar as insatiably thirsty, constantly scorching and darkening faces, or continually watching for and attacking people; Elmalılı suggests an unquenchable thirst that burns humans.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r7.anchor: Kanmak bilmez bir susuz, mütemâdiyen beşer-sûz

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains lawwaha as continuously scorching human faces and making them dark.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r8.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: Mütemâdiyen beşereler kavuran, yüzler karartan mânası mervîdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r6.claim: The commentary renders the phrase as “scorches people.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r7.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r7.claim: Zamakhshari offers the alternative sense “visible to people.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r7.anchor: “İnsanları kavurur” diye çevirdiğimiz 29. âyete “insanlara görünür” şeklinde de mâna verilmiştir (Zemahşerî, IV, 183).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r8.claim: The verse can also picture Hell as a tableau or mirror that reveals itself to the person who deserves it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r8.anchor: Aynı âyet, “Cehennem, orayı hak eden insana kendini gösteren bir tablo, bir aynadır” şeklinde de anlaşılabilir.

ITQAN:v2p335#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p335#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p335#4/r1.claim: Lawwāḥa is glossed as “turning away” or exposed.

ITQAN:v2p385/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p385/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p385/r7.claim: In Azd Shanuʾa usage, lawwāḥa means “burning.”

DAMGHANI:v1p420/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r6.claim: Lawwāḥa means scorching: the fire burns a person until darker than night; it is also called shawāha for their bodies.
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r6.anchor: الثالث : لواحة يعني لفاحة قوله تعالى في سورة المدثر

FARRA:v3p202/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r6.claim: لواحة is nominative by an implicit repeated سقر, like 85:15–16 and Abdullah's reading of 11:72; accusative is also valid.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#9/r1.claim: Lawwāḥa means that it alters the skin; Arabs say the sun “changed” someone when it affected their complexion.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#9/r1.anchor: {لواحة للبشر} أي مغيرة لهم. يقال: لاحته الشمس؛ إذا غيرته.

NAHHAS:v5p67/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r13.claim: لواحة may be a predicate with implicit subject هي; البشر may mean human skin collectively or a plural of بشرة.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r13.anchor: على إضمار مبتدأ أي هي لواحة للبشر أي للخلق

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r1.claim: The common nominative makes لواحة the predicate of omitted هي and supports taking لا تبقي as independent.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بالرفع خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أي: هي لواحة. وهذه مقوية للاستئناف في " لا تبقي "

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي وعطية العوفي
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r2.claim: These readers have لواحة accusative, circumstantial from سقر, لا تبقي, or لا تذر.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي وعطية العوفي بنصبها على الحال، وفيها ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the accusative as specification for emphasis; the commentator calls it emphatic circumstantial since Fire necessarily alters skins.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r3.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري نصبها على الاختصاص للتهويل، وجعلها الشيخ حالا مؤكدة

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن كيسان
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r4.claim: لواحة may mean appearing or shining to people, from لاح يلوح; al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān adopt this sense.

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r5.speaker: جمهور الناس
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r5.claim: Most interpreters derive لواحة from لوحه, discoloring and blackening; a poem about the simoom supports this usage.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r5.anchor: وإليه ذهب جمهور الناس أنها من لوحه، أي: غيره وسوده. قال الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r6.claim: لوحه can mean altering complexion; the cited line يا بنة عمي لاحني الهواجر witnesses the usage, while لوح also denotes severe thirst.

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r7.claim: The poem سقتني على لوح من الماء uses لوح for severe thirst; لوح with ḍamma also names the air between heaven and earth.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r7.anchor: سقتني على لوح من الماء شربة

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r8.claim: البشر may mean human skins, which the Fire discolors, or humanity as a whole.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r8.anchor: والبشر: إما جمع بشرة، أي: مغيرة للجلود،

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r9.claim: The lām in للبشر is an added strengthening particle, as in the cited Yūsuf phrase.

SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r10.claim: The accusative reading supports treating لا تبقي as a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:74:29/r10.anchor: وقراءة النصب في " لواحة " مقوية لكون " لا تبقي " في محل الحال

ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r4.claim: The rendering says hell makes truth visible to mortal man.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r4.anchor: making [all truth] visible to mortal man

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.claim: Asad reads this and Qur'anic descriptions of the hereafter allegorically, as the next verse and verses 28 onward indicate.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.anchor: The allegorical character of this and all other Qur'anic descriptions of man's condition and destiny in the hereafter is clearly alluded to in the subsequent verse

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r1.speaker: Most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r1.claim: Most commentators understand the phrase as changing or scorching human skin.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r1.anchor: Most of the commentators interpret the above elliptic phrase

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r2.claim: Asad follows the primary sense of laha, to appear, shine forth, or become visible, and takes lawwah as that which makes something visible.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r2.anchor: the rendering adopted by me, on the other hand, is based on the primary significance of the verb laha

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r3.claim: The phrase describes the sinner's late recognition of truth, insight into his nature and past wrongs, and realization that he is responsible for his coming suffering.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r3.anchor: it relates to the sinner's belated cognition of the truth, as well as to his distressing insight into his own nature, his past failings

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r4.claim: The sinner's state is neither life nor death, as also expressed at 87:12–13.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n14/r4.anchor: a state neither of life nor of death

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Razin, and most commentators say the fire changes complexions, burns skin, and blackens it; البشر means skin or complexion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو رزين والجمهور: معناه مغيرة للبشرات محرقة للجلود مسودة لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r3.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan derive لواحة from appearing: the enormous, dreadful fire becomes visible to people from five hundred years away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن كيسان: لواحة بناء مبالغة من لاح إذا ظهر، والمعنى أنها تظهر للناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r4.claim: The majority read لواحة in the nominative, understood as a new clause: it is a scorching fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لواحة بالرفع، أي هي لواحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r5.speaker: العوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r5.claim: Al-Awfi, Zayd ibn Ali, Hasan, and Ibn Abi Abla read لواحة in the accusative as an emphatic circumstantial description, since a fire that leaves nothing must alter skin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r5.anchor: وقرأ العوفي وزيد بن علي والحسن وابن أبي عبلة: لواحة بالنصب على الحال المؤكدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the accusative as specification that intensifies the threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p331/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: نصبا على الاختصاص للتهويل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو رزين والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Abū Razīn, and most commentators say Saqar changes the skin’s color and blackens it; some reports add that it burns.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو رزين والجمهور أي مغيرة للبشرات مسودة للجلود وفي بعض الروايات عن بعض بزيادة محرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r2.claim: The word derives from the sun darkening a person’s exposed skin and extremities.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r2.anchor: فلواحة من لوحته الشمس إذا سودت ظاهره وأطرافه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r3.claim: A cited Arabic line uses the related verb for darkening caused by the heat of the noonday sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r3.anchor: يا ابنة عمي لا حني الهواجر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r4.claim: Some reports say the fire flares against skin in a burst, leaving it blacker than night.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنها تلفح الجلد لفحة فتدعه أشد سوادا من الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r5.claim: The apparent tension with “it leaves nothing” can be answered by saying it first blackens and then burns and destroys, or that the descriptions concern those inside it and those near it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r5.anchor: وأجيب أنها في أول الملاقاة تسوده ثم تحرقه وتهلكه أو الأول حالها مع من دخلها وهذا حالها مع من يقرب منها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r6.claim: If both descriptions are treated as the fire’s qualities without a deliberate escalation, blackening is one feature, perhaps of first contact; it is added as a hideous disfigurement beyond pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r6.anchor: من غير قصد إلى ترق من فظيع إلى أفظع وكونها لواحة وصف من أوصافها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r7.claim: On the skin-darkening reading, “al-bashar” may be a collective noun meaning people generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r7.anchor: وجوز على تفسير لواحة بما ذكر كون البشر اسم جنس بمعنى الناس ويرجع المعنى إلى ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r8.speaker: الحسن وابن كيسان والأصم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Kaysān, and al-Aṣamm take “lawwāḥah” as an intensive form of “appear”: it appears to people because of its vastness and terror.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن كسيان والأصم لواحة بناء مبالغة من لاح إذا ظهر والبشر بمعنى الناس أي تظهر للناس لعظمها وهولها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r9.claim: This reading is linked to the verse saying that Hell is brought into view for those who see; a report says it appears from a distance of five hundred years.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r9.anchor: كما قال تعالى وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى وقد جاء أنها تظهر لهم من مسيرة خمسمائة عام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r10.claim: The standard nominative is the predicate of an omitted subject, “it is lowwāḥah.” ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, Zayd b. ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Abī ʿAblah read the accusative for emphasis or as a circumstantial construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r10.anchor: ورفع لواحة على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هي لواحة وقرأ عطية العوفي وزيد بن علي والحسن وابن أبي عبلة لواحة بالنصب على الاختصاص للتهويل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r11.claim: The accusative reading can also be circumstantial from the pronoun in “it leaves/spares” if destruction entails blackening, or from Saqar under the earlier governing verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125#4/r11.anchor: وجوز أن يكون حالا مؤكدة من ضمير تبقي أو تذر بناء على زعم الاستلزام وأن يكون حالا من سقر والعامل ما مر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r5.claim: Lawwāḥah means that the Fire changes the skin and makes it black; Arab usage also says illness or grief changed a person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r5.anchor: {لواحة للبشر} مغيرة للجلد حتى تجعله أسود، يقال: لاحه السقم والحزن إذا غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Fire scorches skin until it becomes darker than night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تلفح الجلد حتى تدعه أشد سوادا من الليل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam explain lawwāḥah as burning the skin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم: محرقة للجلد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r8.speaker: الحسن وابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan say Hell becomes visible to them, comparing this with the verse about Hell being exposed to the deviant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن كيسان: تلوح لهم جهنم حتى يروها عيانا نظيره قوله: "وبرزت الجحيم للغاوين" (الشعراء-91)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r9.claim: Lawwāḥah is nominative as an adjective of Saqar in the question 'what is Saqar?'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r9.anchor: رفع على نعت "سقر" في قوله: "وما أدراك ما سقر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r10.claim: Bashar is the collective of basharah, and its plural is abshār.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p270/r10.anchor: و"البشر" جمع بشرة وجمع البشر أبشار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r1.claim: Lawwāḥa may mean that it blackens the upper skin, or that it is visible to people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r1.anchor: أي مسودة لأعالي الجلد، أو لائحة للناس

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:29-30/r2.claim: The word is also read in the accusative as a specification.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r7.claim: Lawwaha describes intense heat that discolors and damages with blackness, blueness, flashing, convulsion, thirst, and similar effects.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r7.anchor: شديدة التغيير بالسواد والزرقة واللمع والاضطراب والتعطيش ونحوها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r8.claim: In Arab usage, laha al-nar al-shay means that fire scorched and blackened something.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r8.anchor: تقول العرب : لاحت النار الشيء - إذا أحرقته وسودته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r9.claim: Bashar can mean people, or their skin; bashara is singular skin and its plural is abshar.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r9.anchor: أي للناس أو لجلودهم , جمع بشرة وجمع البشر أبشار

DURR-FULL:v8p332/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses lawwāḥa as burning the skin.
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {لواحة للبشر} قال: حراقة للجلد

DURR-FULL:v8p332/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says it scorches and burns the skin until its color changes and becomes blacker than night.
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {لواحة للبشر} قال: تلوح الجلد فتحرقه فيتغير لونه فيصر أسود من الليل

DURR-FULL:v8p332/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r5.speaker: أبو رزين
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r5.claim: Abu Razin says it scorches the skin until it leaves it darker than night.
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r5.anchor: عن أبي رزين {لواحة للبشر} قال: تلوح جلده حتى تدعه أشد سوادا من الليل

DURR-FULL:v8p332/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, through ʿAli, glosses lawwāḥa as burning.
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r6.anchor: من طريق علي عن ابن عباس {لواحة} محرقة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3383/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3383/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3383/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses lawwāḥa as scorching or burning.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3383/r1.anchor: من طريق علي عن ابن عباس لواحة محرقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.claim: The context accommodates these readings through the eloquence of Quranic arrangement; after 74:29 the pronoun would unambiguously refer to Saqar, showing the effect of sentence placement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.anchor: ولو وقعت إثر قوله : { لواحة للبشر } ( المدثر : 29 ) لتمحض ضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، أبو رزين، جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, Abu Razin, and most people say it alters complexions, burns skin, and blackens it; البشر is the plural of بشرة.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو رزين وجمهور الناس: معناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r5.claim: Arabic says fire burned and blackened a thing; al-A'sha's line and Abu Ubayda's rajaz attest this usage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r6.speaker: الحسن، ابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r6.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan derive لواحة from appearing: Saqar becomes visible to people from five hundred years away because of its size, terror, and roaring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن كيسان: لواحة بناء مبالغة من لاح يلوح إذا ظهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r7.speaker: عطية العوفي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r7.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi reads لواحة in the accusative.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r1.claim: Lawwāḥa means changing a person's appearance; the sun is said to have changed him, as a cited verse illustrates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r1.anchor: لواحة أي مغيرة يقال لاحته الشمس أي غيرته وأنشدوا يا ابنة عمي لاحني الهواجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن السميفع، ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r2.claim: They read lawwāḥatan in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن السميفع وابن أبي عبلة لواحة بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r3.speaker: مجاهد، الفراء، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r3.claim: Al-bashar means human skin, the visible outer layer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه جمع بشرة وهي جلدة الإنسان الظاهرة وهذا قول مجاهد والفراء والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r4.speaker: الأخفش، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r4.claim: An alternative takes al-bashar to mean the human beings who are people of the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#7/r4.anchor: والثاني أنهم الإنس من أهل النار قاله الأخفش وابن قتيبة في آخرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r1.claim: Mujahid says lawwāḥa li-l-bashar means that Hell scorches the skin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: أي للجلد، وقال أبو رزين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r2.claim: Abu Razin says the fire flares against the skin, leaving it as black as night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r2.anchor: وقال أبو رزين: تلفح الجلد لفحة فتدعه أسود من الليل. وقال زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the bodies there are made to gleam or show visibly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r3.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: تلوح أجسادهم عليها. وقال قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r4.claim: Qatada explains lawwāḥa li-l-bashar as burning the skin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: {لواحة للبشر} أي: حراقة للجلد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Hell burns a person’s skin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p268/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: تحرق بشرة الإنسان

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r1.claim: The common reading has lawwāḥatun in the nominative as an adjective of Saqar in what is Saqar; it may also be an implied predicate, while ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī reads it accusatively as an adjective of Saqar in sa-uṣlīhi Saqar.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: لواحة بالرفع على أنه نعت للسقر في قوله: ما سقر

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r2.speaker: عطية العوفي
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r2.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī reads lawwāḥatan in the accusative, making it an adjective of Saqar in sa-uṣlīhi Saqar.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r2.anchor: وقرأ عطية العوفي: لواحة بالنصب على أنه نعت لقوله

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r7.claim: Talwīḥ is changing color, as the sun changes a person's complexion; lawwāḥah intensifies the sense of repeated or extreme scorching.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r7.anchor: والتلويح: التغيير للون، لوحته الشمس تلوحه تلويحا

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r8.claim: Basharah is the skin's outer surface, plural bashar; humans are called bashar because their skin is exposed rather than covered in fur or hair.

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r12.claim: Saqar changes the skin's color, especially making the sufferers' complexions very dark.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r12.anchor: للجلود تلوح ألوانهم لا سيما إذا اشتد سوادهم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r13.claim: One view says the tortured person's color changes when he sees Saqar.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r13.anchor: وقيل: إذا شاهدها المعذب تغير لونه

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r14.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r14.claim: Mujāhid says one blast from Saqar scorches the skin and leaves it darker than night.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r14.anchor: قال مجاهد: تلفح الجلد لفحة فتدعه أشد سوادا من الليل

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، وزيد بن أسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Zayd ibn Aslam explain lawwāḥah as burning the skin.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r15.anchor: محرقة للجلود، عن ابن عباس، وزيد بن أسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r16.speaker: الحسن، والأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Aṣamm say Hellfire appears to its victims until they see it with their own eyes.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r16.anchor: تلوح لهم جهنم حتى يروها عيانا، عن الحسن، والأصم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r4.claim: لواحة derives from scorching heat; a cited poem uses لاحك for scorching, and the fire leaves skin blacker than night.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r5.claim: The cited poetic line witnesses the scorching sense of لاحك and لاحنى.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r5.anchor: تقول ما لاحك يا مسافر … يا آبنة عمي لاحنى الهواجر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r6.claim: البشر means the upper layers of skin.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r7.claim: Al-Hasan interprets لواحة as making the fire visible to people, comparing it to seeing Hell with certainty.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r8.claim: A reading puts لواحة in the accusative as emphatic specification, heightening the threat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r16.speaker: أبو رزين
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r16.claim: Abu Razin says lawwaha changes the inmates' color; its flare leaves faces darker than night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r16.anchor: أحدها : مغيرة لألوانهم , قال أبو رزين تلفح وجوههم لفحة تدعهم أشد سوادا من الليل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r17.speaker: عطية
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r17.claim: Atiyya says it burns the skin until the bone shows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r17.anchor: الثاني : تحرق البشر حتى تلوح العظم , قاله عطية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r18.claim: Mujahid says the skin of their bodies is exposed to the fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r18.anchor: الثالث : أن بشرة أجسادهم تلوح على النار , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r19.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r19.claim: Al-Akhfash says lawwaha means intense thirst, so the Fire makes its inmates thirsty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r19.anchor: الرابع : أن اللواح شدة العطش , والمعنى أنها معطشة للبشر , أي لأهلها , قاله الأخفش , وأنشد

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r10.claim: Lawwāḥa means that the Fire burns people.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r10.anchor: { لواحة للبشر } [آية: 29] محرقة للخلق { عليها تسعة عشر }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r1.claim: “لواحة” is the predicate of an omitted subject, “هي”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هي لواحة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r2.claim: “البشر” means skin; the Fire blackens and burns it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#5/r2.anchor: جمع بشرة وهي ظاهر الجلدي أي مسودة للجلود ومحرقة لها

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r10.claim: Lawwaha means changing or disfiguring, from the verb meaning to change.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r10.anchor: أي مغيرة، من لاحه إذا غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r11.claim: The common nominative makes lawwaha an adjective of Saqar; Atiyya al-Awfi, Nasr ibn Asim, and Isa ibn Umar read accusative as emphatic specification.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r12.speaker: أبو رزين
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r12.claim: Abu Razin says its flame scorches faces, leaving them blacker than night; Mujahid also transmits this.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r12.anchor: وقال أبو رزين: تلفح وجوههم لفحة تدعها أشد سوادا من الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r13.claim: Arabic usage says cold, heat, illness, and grief change a person; poetry supports this sense of laaha.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r13.anchor: والعرب تقول: لاحه البرد والحر والسقم والحزن: إذا غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says Saqar is visible to people from five hundred years away.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: { لواحة } أي تلوح للبشر من مسيرة خمسمائة عام

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r15.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r15.claim: Hasan and Ibn Kaysan say Hell appears until people see it plainly.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r15.anchor: الحسن وابن كيسان: تلوح لهم جهنم حتى يروها عيانا

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r16.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash derives the word from thirst: Saqar makes its inhabitants thirsty; poetry uses lawh for severe thirst.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r16.anchor: والمعنى أنها معطشة للبشر أي لأهلها قاله الأخفش

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi connects Hell’s appearance with its being brought into view for the wayward in 26:91.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash and most exegetes take bashar as the human inhabitants of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه الإنس من أهل النار قاله الأخفش والأكثرون

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take bashar as human skin, plural abshar; Ibn Abbas’s distant-visible gloss instead means people because it refers to shining.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29#2/r3.anchor: الثاني أنه جمع بشرة، وهي جلدة الإنسان الظاهرة قاله مجاهد وقتادة
